title: [MIG-001] Reconcile workflow authority and register the Vibez migration
body:
## Objective

Make migration tasks executable under a documented, evidence-backed operating regime, including the one-time seed of an empty Vibez repository.

**Task ID:** MIG-001
**Repository:** Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball
**Canonical branch:** `migration/mig-001-authority-and-task-registration`

- No new implementation prerequisite. Inspect current source authority and the existing bootstrap evidence before changing it.

This issue defines future implementation; creating it does not start a run or grant publication/merge/recovery authority. Read the repository operating instructions, constitution, linked roadmap and affected module contracts. Work only on the canonical branch from the verified base; inspect an existing branch before using it. For an empty Vibez repository, follow MIG-001's reviewed seed protocol rather than pretending main/task infrastructure exists. Cross-repository issue dependencies are admission prerequisites, not invented native DONE records.

## In scope

Read current #1/#37/#74/#75/#78, AGENTS.md, CONSTITUTION.md and BOOTSTRAP.md. At the planning baseline, #37 is closed while main still documents manual bootstrap authority and #1 has unchecked completion criteria. Establish what authority actually applies; coordinate any unfinished cutover acceptance with existing #37 rather than implementing a second bootstrap.
Define how a pinned known-good source engine controls the migration until the installed Vibez artifact can control its own development. Document a narrowly scoped first-commit/seed procedure for empty Vibez, its independent review/CI evidence and subsequent switch to normal task execution; do not pretend the empty repository already runs its own engine.
Prepare schema-valid task/requirement manifests from the linked migration issues, with canonical branch, scope, validators and roles. Stage future tasks without making unresolved cross-repository dependencies eligible. Record external acceptance references and hashes in the supported mechanism; if the registry cannot represent a cross-repo prerequisite, document an explicit audited admission gate rather than inventing DONE records.
Coordinate #78 ownership and the source-delta ledger with MIG-002/003. Preserve the stopped historical canary.

**Expected surfaces:** Root governance/operator docs, migration execution/registration records, tasks/definitions and requirements; issue #1/#37 reconciliation only where justified by evidence.

## Out of scope

No library extraction, package release, canary rerun, arbitrary workflow execution, or fabricated review/completion records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC-01:** Current operating authority and the #37/docs mismatch are resolved or precisely recorded with an actionable prerequisite; issue closure alone is not treated as cutover evidence.
- [ ] **AC-02:** Every planned migration task has a manifest/admission owner and exact repository/branch mapping; invalid, cyclic, missing or unresolved external prerequisites cannot become eligible.
- [ ] **AC-03:** The empty-repository seed protocol, external engine version and one-time exception boundary are reviewable before seed implementation; normal independent review/CI remain required.
- [ ] **AC-04:** A real migration implementation can be assigned and delivered without inventing bootstrap task lifecycle records or treating an ordinary merge as controlled completion.
- [ ] **AC-05:** Live CANARY-001 retirement and historical runtime records remain unchanged.

## Validation and evidence

Validate all authored manifests and references using current schema/contract tooling; audit the dependency graph against issue links. Walk a fresh agent through the start and seed procedure and exercise invalid/unresolved admission cases. Reconcile governance against current main and actual evidence, not the earlier audit summary.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.

## Required reviews and handoff

Require fresh QA, Architecture and UAT/Product review of the final applicable revision. Architecture must inspect changed contracts, upstream dependencies and downstream consumers; UAT must exercise this issue's actual outcome. A developer self-check is not independent approval. The PR links this issue, the roadmap and migration parent, targets main from the canonical branch, and records actual validation/review/CI/controlled-completion evidence under the reconciled operating regime. Creation of these issues does not assign reviewers or authorize a release.

## Rollback

Revert only new registration/guidance if needed; leave append-only task/run/evidence history intact. No broad bootstrap rewrite.

Record completion evidence against #74 and the roadmap only after the removal PR satisfies required review/CI/controlled completion. A rollback reverts the cleanup commit or restores the pinned consumer version under the supported quiescent procedure, not history rewriting.

**Expected surfaces:** Only inventoried migrated paths, consumer scripts/build/CI, AGENTS/README/archive navigation, lightweight consumer integration test and source-reference guard.

## Out of scope

No deletion of project requirements/configuration, runtime/evidence data, Git history or unrelated code; no disabling required validation/review to make cleanup pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC-01:** MIG-009 parity, observation criteria, independent reviews and rollback evidence are accepted before removal starts.
- [ ] **AC-02:** The final removal manifest accounts for every deleted path and retains all project-owned and historical material.
- [ ] **AC-03:** No authoritative duplicate workflow implementation remains; consumer imports/commands resolve only through the pinned supported Vibez surface.
- [ ] **AC-04:** Fresh clone/install and full supported consumer journey work without the deleted source; required CI remains enabled.
- [ ] **AC-05:** Runtime/evidence/history records are unchanged by cleanup, and old archive/source links remain usable.
- [ ] **AC-06:** Ownership/docs and a regression guard prevent future embedded forks; #74 has an evidence-backed completion map.

## Validation and evidence

Review the deletion diff path-by-path against the ownership manifest. Run fresh-install consumer CI/conformance smoke, reference/deep-import scans and history checksum comparison. Demonstrate rollback from the cleanup commit without modifying runtime data.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.

## Required reviews and handoff

Require fresh QA, Architecture and UAT/Product review of the final applicable revision. Architecture must inspect changed contracts, upstream dependencies and downstream consumers; UAT must exercise this issue's actual outcome. A developer self-check is not independent approval. The PR links this issue, the roadmap and migration parent, targets main from the canonical branch, and records actual validation/review/CI/controlled-completion evidence under the reconciled operating regime. Creation of these issues does not assign reviewers or authorize a release.

## Rollback

Revert the cleanup commit if necessary and use MIG-009's stopped-writer procedure. The prior source remains in Git history; never maintain two active implementations.

title: [BOOTSTRAP] Agentic Development System v1 — Master Tracking Plan
body:
# Agentic Development System v1 — Master Tracking Plan

> **Status:** Planning / bootstrap; live canary completion prerequisite retired by owner decision on 2026-11-07
>
> **Purpose of this issue:** This is the temporary source-of-truth tracking document for building the repository's own agentic development system. Until the core task engine exists, GitHub Issues are the authoritative tracker. After the bootstrap reaches v1, the repository-native task system becomes authoritative and this issue becomes the historical parent record.

---

## Owner decision — live canary prerequisite retired (2026-11-07)

The project owner directed: “The canary test served its purpose please help make it no longer required or passed”. The selected disposition is **no longer required**: the remaining live CANARY-001 end-to-end completion and reconciliation are retired as prerequisites for BOOT-034 acceptance, BOOT-035, and Bootstrap v1 cutover. This records a requirements change, not a successful test result.

The observed live lifecycle remains `UAT_REVIEW`; no live controlled merge or `DONE` is claimed. Preserve existing assignments, journals, packets, evidence and lifecycle history. Do not fabricate PASS/DONE records or treat an ordinary merged implementation PR as controlled-completion evidence. Automated canary regression, rehearsal and adversarial coverage remain supported, and required CI, independent review and controlled-merge rules for future work still apply. This decision alone does not declare Bootstrap v1 complete.

## 1. Mission

Build the **development control plane before building fantasy-football product features**.

The bootstrap must create a repository-native system in which an AI agent can be told to "work the next task" and can:

1. determine the next eligible task from an explicit dependency graph;
2. acquire that task without racing another agent;
3. create/use the unique task branch;
4. receive only the role-appropriate context;
5. implement within declared scope;
6. run deterministic development validation;
7. hand the result to independent QA;
8. hand the result to an architecture/integration review with cross-module semantic context;
9. hand the result to UAT/product-intent review;
10. create/update a PR;
11. merge only when every required gate is satisfied;
12. mark the task complete only through the orchestration system; and
13. expose an auditable record of what happened, why it passed, and what should run next.

The design must be **agent-provider agnostic**. ChatGPT/Codex or another agent may drive the workflow, but durable project state, rules, validation, and transitions must live in the repository/GitHub—not in an agent's conversation memory.

---

## 2. Architectural principles to lock during bootstrap

These are the invariants the bootstrap itself must eventually enforce.

### Repository as source of truth
- Project requirements, task dependencies, module contracts, review evidence, and lifecycle state must be inspectable from the repository.
- Agents must not be trusted to remember workflow state.
- Human-readable Markdown and machine-readable manifests/schemas must agree.

### Deterministic control plane
- AI may write code, reason about requirements, and perform semantic reviews.
- AI must **not** be the authority that decides whether deterministic gates passed.
- State transitions must be made by the CLI/orchestrator after verifiable prerequisites are satisfied.

### Strict role separation
- **Developer:** local implementation context; builds the requested change.
- **QA reviewer:** validates behavior against task acceptance criteria and failure cases.
- **Architecture reviewer:** deliberately receives broader dependency/consumer context and checks semantic system fit, not merely type compatibility.
- **UAT/Product reviewer:** checks that the delivered behavior achieves the intended user outcome and original requirement.
- **Merge controller:** performs no implementation judgment; it merges only when required evidence is green.

A role may be executed by the same underlying model at different times, but it must receive a fresh role-specific context package and must not be allowed to self-approve its own implementation.

### Semantic contracts, not only type contracts
Module interfaces must capture:
- structural contract (types/schema);
- capability contract (what the module promises it can do);
- behavioral constraints and ranges;
- invariants;
- known consumers;
- consumer expectations/assumptions;
- examples and edge cases.

Architecture review must ask not only "does this compile?" but also "does the changed producer still satisfy what downstream consumers actually need?"

### Explicit scope
Every task must eventually declare:
- objective;
- in scope;
- out of scope;
- dependencies;
- allowed/expected file areas;
- requirements;
- acceptance criteria;
- validation plan;
- affected contracts/consumers;
- required review roles.

### Evidence before status
No agent manually checks a "done" box.
A task reaches completion because the system has recorded the required evidence and transitioned it through the state machine.

### Recoverable and idempotent
Re-running a command must not corrupt project state.
Interrupted work must be resumable.
Failed reviews must return the task to a defined rework state without losing previous evidence.

### Pluggable boundaries
The bootstrap should define interfaces around:
- agent runner/provider;
- source-control/GitHub operations;
- persistence/state store;
- validation executors;
- review roles/context builders.

The first implementation may be GitHub-centric, but the core domain should not hard-code a single agent vendor.

---

## 3. Provisional bootstrap technology stance

These choices are **directional for the bootstrap** and can be refined in child implementation issues:

- **Primary language:** TypeScript
- **Runtime:** Node.js
- **Human control surface:** CLI
- **Human project/product UI:** deferred until after bootstrap
- **Machine-readable definitions:** JSON/YAML validated by versioned schemas
- **Human-readable definitions:** Markdown adjacent to manifests/specs
- **Automation/CI:** GitHub Actions
- **Source control:** Git + GitHub PRs
- **Bootstrap tracker:** GitHub Issues until the repository-native tracker is operational
- **Long-term agent invocation:** provider-neutral runner interface with adapters

CSV/JSON export remains a product-level design goal for fantasy analysis, but it is not part of the agentic bootstrap itself.

---

## 4. Proposed lifecycle / state machine

The implementation issue for the state machine will define exact transition rules, but the bootstrap should converge on a lifecycle broadly equivalent to:

`PLANNED`
→ `READY`
→ `ASSIGNED`
→ `IN_DEVELOPMENT`
→ `DEV_VALIDATED`
→ `QA_REVIEW`
→ `ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW`
→ `UAT_REVIEW`
→ `MERGE_READY`
→ `MERGED`
→ `DONE`

Failure/recovery states should include at least:

- `BLOCKED`
- `DEV_VALIDATION_FAILED`
- `QA_FAILED`
- `ARCHITECTURE_FAILED`
- `UAT_FAILED`
- `MERGE_BLOCKED`
- `REWORK_REQUIRED`

A failed review returns control to development with structured findings. A new implementation revision invalidates stale downstream approvals when the changed surface makes those approvals no longer trustworthy.

---

## 5. Branch and task conventions

### Task IDs
Bootstrap tasks use stable IDs:

`BOOT-000`, `BOOT-001`, ...

Future product tasks should use their own domain prefix.

### Branches
Every implementation task gets exactly one canonical branch:

`bootstrap/<task-id>-<short-slug>`

Examples:
- `bootstrap/boot-005-cli-shell`
- `bootstrap/boot-016-architecture-review`

The task/lock record must identify its canonical branch. The branch name is part of the assignment identity and may not be silently replaced.

### Parent tracking
This issue is the **bootstrap epic/master tracker**.
Each checklist item below will later receive its own implementation issue/spec before work begins.

---

# 6. Phased implementation plan

## Phase 0 — Manual seed and repository constitution

**Goal:** Create the minimum trustworthy skeleton from which the automated system can build itself.

- [x] **BOOT-000 — Seed repository skeleton and bootstrap constitution**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-000-seed-constitution`  
  Establish the initial directories, root governance documents, bootstrap version marker, and immutable architectural invariants required to build the rest of the system.

- [x] **BOOT-001 — Root agent operating instructions**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-001-agent-instructions`  
  Define the mandatory workflow an agent must follow when entering the repository: discover task through CLI, never self-select arbitrary work, respect scope, validate, hand off, and never self-mark completion.

- [x] **BOOT-002 — Role model and review authority definitions**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-002-role-model`  
  Formalize Developer, QA, Architect, UAT/Product, and Merge Controller responsibilities, context visibility, prohibited actions, and approval authority.

- [x] **BOOT-003 — Core schemas and versioning policy**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-003-core-schemas`  
  Establish versioned machine-readable schemas for tasks, requirements, lifecycle state, locks/assignments, review results, validation evidence, and module/consumer contracts.

- [x] **BOOT-004 — Module semantic contract standard**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-004-module-contracts`  
  Define the standard README/manifest bundle each future module/provider/adapter must expose, including capabilities, structural interfaces, semantic constraints, consumers, assumptions, and allowed dependencies.

**Phase exit:** The repository has a constitution and schemas sufficient for later code to validate its own workflow definitions.

---

## Phase 1 — CLI foundation and task graph

**Goal:** Make "what should be worked next?" a deterministic repository query instead of an agent judgment.

- [x] **BOOT-005 — CLI application shell and command contract**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-005-cli-shell`  
  Create the stable agent-facing CLI entry point, command naming conventions, structured output contract, exit-code contract, and human-readable diagnostics.

- [x] **BOOT-006 — Task registry loader and schema validation**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-006-task-registry`  
  Load task definitions from the repository, reject malformed/unknown schema versions, and expose normalized task records.

- [x] **BOOT-007 — Dependency DAG validator and resolver**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-007-dependency-dag`  
  Validate task dependencies, reject cycles/missing references, and compute dependency satisfaction.

- [x] **BOOT-008 — Next-eligible-task selection**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-008-next-task`  
  Implement deterministic eligibility and priority selection so `agent next` produces the correct task rather than relying on model interpretation.

- [x] **BOOT-009 — Lifecycle state transition engine**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-009-state-machine`  
  Implement explicit allowed transitions, transition prerequisites, rejection reasons, and state history.

**Phase exit:** The CLI can validate the project task graph and report the single next eligible task (or a clear blocked/empty result).

---

## Phase 2 — Assignment, branch identity, locking, and context compilation

**Goal:** Allow an agent to safely start work and receive the correct bounded context.

- [x] **BOOT-010 — Task assignment and lock manager**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-010-assignment-locks`  
  Atomically assign a task, create/record lock ownership, detect stale/conflicting assignments, and support explicit release/recovery.

- [x] **BOOT-011 — Git branch lifecycle adapter**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-011-branch-lifecycle`  
  Enforce canonical task branch naming, branch creation/verification, base-ref expectations, and branch/task identity checks.

- [x] **BOOT-012 — Role-aware context compiler**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-012-context-compiler`  
  Compile a task bundle containing only the information appropriate to the current role: task spec, required documents, permitted scope, dependencies, contracts, examples, and review instructions.

- [x] **BOOT-013 — Developer task-start workflow**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-013-dev-start`  
  Combine next-task resolution, lock acquisition, branch checks, and developer context generation into the canonical command used to begin implementation.

**Phase exit:** An agent can start the next task safely, on the correct branch, with reproducible role-scoped instructions.

---

## Phase 3 — Deterministic validation and evidence

**Goal:** Replace "the developer says it works" with machine-verifiable evidence.

- [x] **BOOT-014 — Validation executor framework**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-014-validation-framework`  
  Define the extensible framework for running required checks (tests, lint/type checks, schema checks, contract checks, repository invariants, and task-specific validators).

- [x] **BOOT-015 — Evidence and review artifact store**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-015-evidence-store`  
  Record validation inputs/results, commit SHA, timestamps, task/revision identity, failures, reviewer outputs, and invalidation relationships in an auditable form.

- [x] **BOOT-016 — Developer validation gate**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-016-dev-validation`  
  Implement the canonical `validate dev implementation` gate. It may advance the task only when required deterministic evidence is present and green.

**Phase exit:** Development cannot hand off work without reproducible validation evidence tied to the exact revision under review.

---

## Phase 4 — Independent review pipeline

**Goal:** Evaluate the same change from deliberately different perspectives.

- [x] **BOOT-017 — Generic review framework and structured findings**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-017-review-framework`  
  Establish role-independent review invocation, PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED semantics, severity, findings, evidence references, and remediation records.

- [x] **BOOT-018 — QA review workflow**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-018-qa-review`  
  Give QA the requirements, acceptance criteria, revision, and necessary test context. QA validates correctness, edge cases, negative cases, and regression behavior without relying on the developer's self-assessment.

- [x] **BOOT-019 — Architecture / semantic dependency review**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-019-architecture-review`  
  Give the architect broader producer-and-consumer context. Review structural compatibility, capability/range changes, semantic behavior, dependency direction, architectural invariants, and whether downstream consumers can still satisfy their own acceptance criteria.

- [x] **BOOT-020 — UAT / product-intent review**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-020-uat-review`  
  Validate the feature from the intended user/system outcome backward: does the implemented behavior actually solve the original requirement, including realistic usage scenarios that unit-level QA may miss?

- [x] **BOOT-021 — Review rework and approval invalidation loop**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-021-review-rework`  
  Route failures back to development with structured findings; track revisions; determine which earlier approvals remain valid and which must be re-run after code changes.

**Phase exit:** A task can move from dev validation through QA, architecture, and UAT with independent context and explicit evidence.

---

## Phase 5 — GitHub PR, CI, and merge control

**Goal:** Make GitHub the enforceable integration boundary while preserving the repository-native state model.

- [x] **BOOT-022 — Pull-request lifecycle integration**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-022-pr-lifecycle`  
  Create/update the task PR, link task identity and evidence, preserve branch mapping, and keep PR metadata synchronized with workflow state.

- [x] **BOOT-023 — GitHub Actions CI enforcement**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-023-ci-enforcement`  
  Run repository invariants, schemas, tests, validation checks, task/branch checks, and evidence consistency checks in CI so local agent claims cannot bypass integration rules.

- [x] **BOOT-024 — Merge-readiness policy engine**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-024-merge-policy`  
  Compute merge readiness from CI, exact-head revision, required review evidence, unresolved blocking findings, branch/task identity, dependency state, and any required human gate.

- [x] **BOOT-025 — Controlled merge and completion transition**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-025-controlled-merge`  
  Merge only through the controller, verify the PR head did not move after approval, finalize audit evidence, release the lock, and transition the task to DONE.

**Phase exit:** No task can be merged through the supported workflow unless every required gate is green for the exact code being merged.

---

## Phase 6 — Agent runner and orchestration

**Goal:** Allow a centralized runner to execute the role pipeline without coupling the control plane to one model vendor.

- [x] **BOOT-026 — Agent runner/provider interface**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-026-agent-runner-interface`  
  Define the provider-neutral contract for starting a role session, passing compiled context, receiving structured results, handling tool permissions, and identifying a run.

- [x] **BOOT-027 — Sequential orchestration engine**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-027-orchestration-engine`  
  Coordinate Developer → deterministic validation → QA → Architect → UAT → merge-controller transitions, while delegating all authoritative state changes to the task engine.

- [x] **BOOT-028 — Retry, timeout, cancellation, and idempotency behavior**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-028-runner-resilience`  
  Make interrupted or duplicated runner executions safe; distinguish infrastructure failure from review failure; support resumption without double-transitioning or duplicate merge behavior.

- [x] **BOOT-029 — Initial local/manual agent adapter**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-029-local-agent-adapter`  
  Provide the first usable adapter for handing role context to an external/desktop AI session and ingesting its structured result, without making that adapter part of the domain model.

**Phase exit:** The entire workflow can be driven by one orchestration command while remaining replaceable at the agent-provider boundary.

---

## Phase 7 — Visibility, diagnostics, and recovery

**Goal:** Make project state obvious to a human and actionable to an agent.

- [x] **BOOT-030 — Project status and next-work reporting**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-030-status-reporting`  
  Provide CLI views for current phase/task state, blockers, active locks, review status, dependency reasons, and the next eligible work.

- [x] **BOOT-031 — Workflow diagnostics and explainability**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-031-workflow-diagnostics`  
  Add commands that explain why a transition/task is blocked, which requirement/evidence is missing, and what exact remediation is necessary.

- [x] **BOOT-032 — Recovery and administrative repair procedures**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-032-recovery-tools`  
  Define safe recovery for stale locks, abandoned branches, corrupted/incomplete runs, interrupted reviews, and legitimate administrator overrides with an explicit audit trail.

**Phase exit:** A maintainer can answer "where are we, why are we blocked, and what happens next?" without reconstructing state from chat logs.

---

## Phase 8 — Canary, adversarial testing, and v1 cutover

**Goal:** Prove that the bootstrap can safely build future features before making it mandatory.

- [x] **BOOT-035 — Bootstrap hardening, documentation, and v1 cutover**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-035-v1-cutover`  
  Reconcile docs with actual behavior, remove temporary bootstrap exceptions, document operator/agent workflows, define backward-compatible schema policy, and declare the repository-native task system authoritative for all future work.
- **BOOT-033 — End-to-end canary task (live completion prerequisite retired)**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-033-canary-e2e`  
  Retain the implemented canary driver, regression tests, rehearsal and observed live-run evidence. The owner retired the remaining live controlled-merge/DONE and reconciliation requirement on 2026-11-07; it is no longer a cutover blocker and is not reported as passed.

- [x] **BOOT-034 — Negative-path and adversarial workflow tests**  
  Branch: `bootstrap/boot-034-adversarial-tests`  
  Prove the system rejects or safely recovers from cycle dependencies, wrong branches, duplicate assignments, stale locks, failed tests, self-approval attempts, changed PR heads, semantic-review failures, malformed evidence, and bypass attempts.


**Phase exit / Bootstrap v1:** Automated canary regression and negative-path tests are green, the remaining v1 completion criteria below are satisfied, and future feature work is prohibited from bypassing the new task system except through explicit audited emergency override. A completed live canary run is no longer required under the owner decision above.

---

# 7. Dependency structure

High-level dependency order:

```text
Phase 0: Constitution + schemas
        ↓
Phase 1: CLI + task DAG + state machine
        ↓
Phase 2: assignment + branch + context
        ↓
Phase 3: deterministic validation + evidence
        ↓
Phase 4: QA + architecture + UAT + rework
        ↓
Phase 5: PR + CI + merge control
        ↓
Phase 6: runner/orchestration
        ↓
Phase 7: visibility + diagnostics + recovery
        ↓
Phase 8: canary + adversarial tests + cutover
```

Child issues may identify safe parallelism inside a phase, but no implementation issue may silently weaken an upstream invariant to make downstream work easier.

---

# 8. Required architecture-review perspective

The **Architecture review is intentionally different from QA**.

For every affected module, it must be able to inspect:

1. the module's declared structural and semantic contract;
2. the changed implementation surface;
3. direct upstream dependencies;
4. direct downstream consumers;
5. downstream consumer requirements and acceptance criteria that depend on this capability;
6. behavioral/range changes even when public types are unchanged;
7. cross-layer dependency rules and architectural invariants.

Example class of failure this must catch:

> A provider still returns the same type, so unit tests and type checks pass, but its implementation narrows the range of possible outputs. A downstream consumer relies on values in the removed range to satisfy its own feature requirements. The contract is structurally unchanged but the system is semantically broken.

That is an **Architecture FAIL**, even if QA for the producer itself passes.

---

# 9. Context-isolation policy

The context compiler must intentionally differ by role.

### Developer receives
- assigned task and local requirement context;
- relevant module contract;
- direct dependency contracts needed to implement;
- explicit allowed scope and prohibited scope;
- acceptance criteria and deterministic validation requirements.

### QA receives
- requirement and acceptance-criteria context;
- code/diff under test;
- supported test fixtures/interfaces;
- prior deterministic validation evidence;
- not the developer's narrative justification unless specifically required as evidence.

### Architect receives
- task and change diff;
- affected module contract;
- dependency graph around the affected surface;
- relevant consumer contracts/requirements;
- architectural invariants and dependency policies;
- QA result as evidence, not as authority.

### UAT/Product receives
- original objective/user outcome;
- acceptance scenarios;
- relevant exposed behavior;
- enough system context to judge outcome;
- not internal implementation details unless required to exercise the behavior.

### Merge controller receives
- merge-readiness facts only;
- it does not reinterpret requirements.

---

# 10. Definition of Bootstrap v1 complete

Bootstrap v1 is **not complete** merely because the CLI exists.

All of the following must be true:

- [ ] Task definitions and lifecycle state are schema validated.
- [ ] Dependency cycles and unsatisfied dependencies cannot be silently ignored.
- [ ] `next` deterministically identifies eligible work.
- [ ] Assignments are lock-protected and branch-bound.
- [ ] Role-specific context is reproducible.
- [ ] Developer validation produces commit-bound evidence.
- [ ] QA is independent of developer self-approval.
- [ ] Architecture review evaluates semantic consumer impact.
- [ ] UAT validates original user/system intent.
- [ ] Rework invalidates stale approvals appropriately.
- [ ] PR/CI status cannot be bypassed by a local agent assertion.
- [ ] Merge readiness is computed for the exact PR head being merged.
- [ ] Only the controlled merge path transitions a task to DONE.
- [ ] Interrupted orchestration can be resumed safely.
- [ ] Project status/blockers/next work are visible through CLI.
- **Retired requirement (2026-11-07):** A real canary task completes end-to-end with no manual state edits. Remaining live completion is no longer required; no PASS/DONE is asserted.
- [ ] Negative-path tests demonstrate that expected bypasses fail safely.
- [ ] Documentation reflects the implementation.
- [ ] The repository-native task system is declared the source of truth for future development.

---

# 11. Explicitly out of scope for this bootstrap epic

These belong to later product epics once the development control plane is operational:

- fantasy-football player/stat database;
- Yahoo ingestion;
- free-data-provider integrations;
- injury/news ingestion;
- projections;
- trade analysis;
- waiver analysis;
- lineup optimization;
- auction tools;
- Flock or other messaging integrations;
- React product UI;
- production fantasy analytics persistence;
- automated football-data notifications.

The bootstrap may define reusable architectural conventions those systems will later follow, but it must not begin implementing them.

---

# 12. Child-issue creation policy

Before any BOOT task is implemented, create a dedicated child issue/spec for it containing:

- parent link to this issue;
- exact objective;
- detailed in/out scope;
- dependencies by task ID;
- authoritative docs/context;
- expected files/surfaces;
- interface and schema decisions;
- detailed acceptance criteria;
- pseudocode/test scenarios;
- deterministic validation requirements;
- required review roles;
- risk/rollback notes;
- canonical branch name from this tracker.

This master issue owns **sequence and architectural intent**. Child issues own **implementation detail**.

---

# 13. Senior-architecture guardrails for the implementation phase

1. **Do not overbuild the bootstrap UI.** The CLI is the agent control plane; product UI comes later.
2. **Do not encode agent prompts as business logic.** Prompts are adapters/configuration; state transitions and checks are code.
3. **Do not store authoritative state only in free-form Markdown.** Human docs should map to validated machine state.
4. **Do not let Git branch presence equal assignment ownership.** Assignment/lock must be explicit.
5. **Do not let a reviewer approve a moving target.** Evidence/approval must bind to an exact revision.
6. **Do not treat a passing type contract as semantic compatibility.**
7. **Do not let role isolation prevent architecture review from seeing consumer intent.**
8. **Do not make GitHub the domain model.** GitHub is the first source-control/CI adapter; the workflow domain should remain testable independently.
9. **Do not add fantasy product features to bootstrap branches.**
10. **Prefer a small, enforceable v1 over a broad workflow with unenforced conventions.**

---

## Immediate next action

Create the detailed child issue for **BOOT-000 — Seed repository skeleton and bootstrap constitution**. That child issue should be the final manually planned bootstrap implementation task before the repository begins using its own progressively-built control plane.

title: [BOOT-035] Bootstrap hardening, documentation, and v1 cutover
body:
## AGENT INSTRUCTIONS — READ FIRST

1. **Read the master bootstrap architecture issue in full before making changes:** [#1 — Agentic Development System v1 — Master Tracking Plan](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/issues/1).
2. **Work only this task.** The master issue and this child issue define scope; do not silently add later product work or redesign earlier components.
3. **Check out exactly this canonical branch:** `bootstrap/boot-035-v1-cutover`. Create it from current `main` only if it does not exist.
4. Confirm all dependencies below are present and accepted on `main`. If not, stop and report the dependency blocker.
5. Implement the smallest coherent change that satisfies this task and preserves all architectural invariants from #1.
6. **Validate the code against every acceptance criterion below.** Run all relevant tests/checks and add focused automated coverage for required happy and negative paths.
7. Re-read the final diff for scope leakage, role-boundary violations, stale evidence assumptions, and semantic downstream regressions.
8. Commit and push `bootstrap/boot-035-v1-cutover`.
9. **After validation passes, create a Pull Request from `bootstrap/boot-035-v1-cutover` into `main`.** Link this issue and #1, summarize evidence, and include `Closes #<this issue number>`.
10. Do not self-declare completion. Use the repository-native review/merge lifecycle implemented by this stage, with GitHub PR/CI as the integration boundary.

> Parent: [#1 — Bootstrap Master Tracking Plan](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/issues/1)  
> Task ID: **BOOT-035**  
> Canonical branch: `bootstrap/boot-035-v1-cutover`

## Objective

Reconcile the implemented control plane with its documentation, remove bootstrap-only exceptions, harden operator/agent workflows, and formally make the repository-native task system authoritative for future development.

## Dependencies

- BOOT-034 (including its automated canary test scaffolding).
