title: [EPIC] Conversational planning and end-to-end workflow API
body:
## Purpose and planning boundary

Give the separate household/project UI a supported API for the **whole development workflow**, starting with a discussion that turns an incomplete idea into a reviewable task plan, then carrying approved work through execution, independent review, PR/CI, controlled completion, and understandable status/evidence.

The planning experience must be iterative: the agent asks questions, incorporates answers and corrections, identifies unresolved decisions, and revises a structured plan. A single prompt that immediately launches execution does not satisfy this epic. An interview is one possible interaction style, not a fixed questionnaire requirement.

This is a **new feature implementation epic**, not a canary/test workload. Only this epic is being established now. Child issues, task decomposition, canonical implementation branches, and detailed endpoint/schema decisions will be planned separately. This issue does not authorize beginning implementation, creating a UI repository, or changing bootstrap completion records.

## Outcomes and scope

- A UI can connect to an explicitly configured local project, discover capabilities and readiness, and inspect what is actually supported.
- A user can start, continue, revisit, and revise a planning conversation, then review a versioned human-readable and machine-readable task plan before it becomes executable work.
- An approved plan can be materialized into valid repository-native requirements/tasks with dependency and acceptance traceability, without silently starting execution or publishing unrelated GitHub content.
- The UI can request authorized execution and resume, observe progress and blockers, inspect current/stale evidence, and follow the existing review/rework/PR/CI/controlled-merge workflow.
- Localhost is the first deployment. Remote and scheduled execution are later adapters around the same application contracts, rather than separate workflow implementations.

### Explicit exclusions

- Building the household/project frontend or its application domain in this repository.
- Moving/publishing the reusable library, choosing its new repository/package name, or duplicating extraction work owned by the companion migration epic.
- Replacing the existing deterministic lifecycle, evidence, review, selection, assignment, or merge rules.
- A general shell endpoint, arbitrary filesystem browser, arbitrary state-editor API, or a chat message that can mark work approved/DONE.
- A hosted multi-tenant service, remote authentication platform, distributed scheduler, unattended spending, or production remote/scheduled deployment in the localhost milestone.
- Resolving or closing the existing bootstrap readiness/cutover issues as a side effect of this feature.
- Creating subtasks in this planning pass.

## Current-code audit

Audited `main` at [`94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe`](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/commit/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe). Read the root operating rules/constitution, current bootstrap authority, relevant source contracts, schemas and operating docs. The repository has no issue template or more-local AGENTS file in the inspected tree.

| Need | Existing foundation and confirmed gap |
| --- | --- |
| Planning discussion and structured drafts | No planning-session/conversation/plan schema or planning service exists in the inspected source/schema tree. [AgentProvider](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/src/agent-provider/agent-provider.ts) currently accepts task/revision-bound execution/review roles, not an unplanned project conversation. Reuse provider-neutral principles, but do not pretend this is already a planner or weaken review-role boundaries. |
| Reviewable task output and publication | [Task schema](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/schemas/v1/task.schema.json), requirement schema, and dependency-DAG validation are reusable. [Task registry](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/src/task-registry/registry.ts) loads/validates existing files; it does not author or approve them. A safe plan-to-task publication boundary is new work. |
| Whole-workflow commands | [CLI core](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/src/cli/core.ts) exposes selected commands, not a UI service. Generic review/rework/orchestration commands remain reserved in [CLI docs](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/docs/CLI.md). This is an application-composition gap, not a reason to rewrite the underlying gates. |
| Execution and recovery | [SequentialOrchestrationEngine](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/src/orchestration-engine/orchestration-engine.ts) already composes start, developer/provider work, validation, required reviews, rework, readiness and controlled merge. Its durable [run store](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/src/orchestration-engine/run-store.ts) preserves identity and repository-wide exclusion. A UI-safe asynchronous supervisor, operation lookup, and general PR-publication integration are not supplied by the generic CLI. |
| Visibility and intervention | [Status](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/docs/STATUS.md), diagnostics, evidence history, local/manual provider exchange, and bounded recovery exist. Status is expressly local registered-task observation, not global GitHub truth or gate approval. There is no inspected HTTP transport, resumable client-event contract, or safe artifact/log resource API. |
| Portability | The private TypeScript/Node package contains module entrypoints and repository-local composition. Stable exports, runtime assets and install/configuration portability belong to the companion migration epic. |

Existing issues #1 and #2–#37 cover bootstrap capabilities, not this combined conversational-planning/UI API epic. Issue and open-PR searches found no existing equivalent to reuse.

### Readiness caveat

At planning time, #35 and #36 are closed, but main's README/BOOTSTRAP/CANARY documentation and #1 still contain pending live-acceptance/checklist statements; #37 remains open. A closed issue alone does not establish reconciled cutover. Refresh these facts and follow the authority actually in force before implementation. Reconciliation belongs to the existing bootstrap work. This epic neither declares cutover nor requires its own feature changes to be canary tasks.

## Recommended architecture and boundaries

**Proposed default, subject to the later child-planning decisions:** a transport-neutral TypeScript workflow application service, with a thin versioned localhost HTTP/JSON adapter and a documented client contract. Use polling for a complete baseline; add replayable event delivery where needed for an interactive UI. Keep transport DTOs separate from internal persistence and gate interfaces.

Data flow:

1. Configured project/context → durable planning conversation → proposed plan revisions.
2. Human review/corrections → explicit acceptance of an exact plan version → validated task/requirement publication.
3. Separately authorized execution request → durable operation supervisor → existing task/role/gate modules.
4. Authoritative state/evidence plus correlated operational events → UI read models, diagnostics and permitted artifacts.

The service is the composition boundary, not a second lifecycle engine. CLI and HTTP must share domain behavior where they expose the same operation. No subprocess parsing of human CLI output and no direct authoritative-state writes from route handlers.

### Planning and publication

- Use stable session, message, plan and revision identities; retain the rationale/assumptions, unresolved questions, decisions and source references needed to review the output. Conversation is context, not proof that a gate passed.
- A session supports multiple question/answer/revision rounds, follow-up after a draft, durable reopen, and explicit abandonment. Changes produce a new plan version/diff rather than silently altering an accepted plan.
- The structured plan must describe objective, in/out scope, requirements, acceptance criteria, tasks, dependencies, canonical branches, allowed paths, validation plan, affected contracts and required review roles. Reuse existing task/requirement schema fields; version any additional envelope or extension deliberately.
- Keep proposed tasks outside the active registry until acceptance/publication. Validate schema, task-ID collisions, missing/cyclic dependencies, referenced requirements/contracts, scope and host policy before any visible publication.
- Approval binds the exact plan version/content and project/repository context. Changed plan or stale repository assumptions require explicit re-review or a visible conflict, not silent execution.
- Materialization must be atomic or recoverably staged so a partial task graph cannot become eligible. Retries cannot duplicate IDs/files/issues. Never overwrite existing task definitions or rewrite a running task implicitly.
- Repository-native artifacts are the proposed default output. Optional GitHub issue synchronization is an adapter and separately authorized external publication, not the definition of the domain.
- The planner proposes; deterministic validators and the user review boundary decide whether a plan can be published. A planning provider must not be shoehorned into QA/UAT/Developer identities or fabricate their approvals.

### UI-facing operations and long-running work

The exact routes are deferred, but the contract must cover capabilities/project readiness; planning sessions/messages/drafts/revisions; plan validation/acceptance/publication; registered task/requirement/dependency views; execution request/status/resume/cancellation; review/rework and required input; PR/CI/merge readiness; evidence/history/log/artifact reads; and diagnostics/recovery guidance.

- Return stable operation IDs for long work rather than keeping an HTTP request alive for the whole workflow. Persist request identity and intended scope before dispatch.
- Scope execution to the approved project and task/plan selection. Do not let the current next-task selector accidentally start unrelated registry work.
- Preserve original owner/run/idempotency identities on retry or resume, including restart and uncertain-outcome reconciliation. Preserve current repository-wide writer exclusion; parallelism requires a separate reviewed workspace-isolation design.
- Distinguish accepted/running/waiting/blocked/failed/cancel-requested/stopped/completed operation observations from authoritative task lifecycle. A browser disconnect is not a cancellation; a cancellation request is not proof external tools stopped.
- Reuse role-specific context, independent judgments, deterministic validation, current-head evidence and controlled merge. Expose needed human input without accepting browser-supplied PASS/DONE or bypass flags.
- Plan acceptance, task publication, execution, external PR publication and merge authority are distinct policy decisions. Use configured authorization and existing governance; do not bake a mandatory extra confirmation into operations already validly authorized.
- Recovery remains bounded, audited and quiescence-aware. Start with diagnostics/guidance where a safe online action is unsupported; never turn a generic API retry into lock stealing or JSON repair.

### Read models, events and local security

- Correlate project/session/plan/task/run/role/revision/operation/evidence identities. Return observation time, provenance and evidence currency; distinguish local branch facts, remote PR/CI facts and unknown/stale data.
- Provide bounded, ordered event/log pagination and reconnect cursors with an explicit expired-cursor/resync behavior. Events and summaries are observations, never authoritative approval records.
- Expose only allowlisted, size-bounded artifacts/logs through stable resource IDs. Redact credentials and private provider internals; do not expose unrestricted paths, environment dumps or hidden model reasoning.
- Bind localhost only by default. Protect browser access with an explicit local session/authorization handshake, host/origin checks, restrictive CORS and CSRF/rebinding defenses appropriate to the chosen transport.
- Resolve project IDs against trusted host configuration rather than accepting arbitrary roots/commands. Validate path containment including symlink escapes; bound request size, concurrency, agent turns/time and log retention.
- Credentials, provider policies and command/executor configuration stay server-side. Generated plan text and external content are untrusted data, not authority to widen tools, network access or execution scope.

### Why this approach

A thin CLI wrapper is quicker initially but does not solve durable interactive planning, asynchronous control, restart-safe client state or safe resource access. A new all-in-one workflow backend would duplicate mature gates and risk divergent policy. A separate transport-neutral application service reuses current modules and stays compatible with library extraction. HTTP/JSON is the proposed first UI transport; GraphQL, WebSockets and distributed workers are not prerequisites.

## Relationship to the migration epic

Companion: [#74 — Package the control-plane library for repository migration](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/issues/74).

- Migration owns supported package exports, assets/schema loading, host/project configuration seams, portable distribution, second-repository installation and compatibility/rollback.
- This epic owns planning domain/service contracts, safe task publication, workflow application composition, API transport, operation supervision and UI observability.
- Agree the shared service-facing exports/configuration contract first. API development can begin in the source repository against that boundary; it need not wait for the final repository move.
- Migration then proves the same consumer works against the installed package. This API must not deep-import source paths or duplicate packaged schemas.
- Do not make the epics mutually blocking. Core contract/configuration seams precede parallel API and packaging work; final installed-consumer compatibility joins them.
- Remote and schedule adapters must invoke the same commands with scoped identities, idempotency and policy. Define seams and contract tests now; choose deployment, identity, scheduling/misfire and concurrency policy before any later production adapter.

## Master acceptance criteria

All criteria remain unchecked. Child ownership and detailed test mapping will be added in a later planning pass.

- [ ] **API-AC-01 — Iterative planning:** A client can complete at least two question/answer/refinement rounds, change an earlier answer, reopen after restart, and obtain a revised draft that preserves decisions and unresolved questions. No work is executed by merely chatting.
- [ ] **API-AC-02 — Reviewable output:** A versioned machine-readable plan and readable view agree, cover the required task/requirement fields, show changes between revisions, and trace tasks/acceptance criteria to original goals. Unsupported or incomplete plans are visibly non-executable.
- [ ] **API-AC-03 — Safe publication:** Accepting and publishing an exact plan creates one valid, auditable task/requirement graph. Stale approval, duplicate IDs, bad references, cycles, disallowed scope and interrupted/duplicate publication are rejected or reconciled without partial eligible work or overwritten tasks.
- [ ] **API-AC-04 — Complete supported workflow:** Through the documented API/client, approved scope can enter assignment/development, validation, independent QA/Architecture/UAT as required, rework, PR/CI, readiness and controlled completion using existing owners. Unsupported actions are explicit capability/blocker results, never simulated success.
- [ ] **API-AC-05 — Durable execution control:** Long operations survive client disconnect and host restart; same-key retry/resume preserves identity without duplicate dispatch, review records, PRs or merges. Concurrent writers, changed scope under the same key and uncertain external outcomes fail safely or reconcile through owning modules.
- [ ] **API-AC-06 — Honest cancellation/intervention:** Timeout, cooperative cancellation, failed review, provider failure and waiting for input remain distinct. External work that may still be active is reported as such; recovery cannot bypass quiescence, assignment or authorization requirements.
- [ ] **API-AC-07 — Useful visibility:** Task/run/role progress, dependencies, blockers/remediation, current/stale evidence, PR/CI facts and permitted artifacts/logs are accessible with stable identities and provenance. Reconnect/pagination does not silently lose history or infer approval from events.
- [ ] **API-AC-08 — Safe localhost host:** An independent client can use the local service, while untrusted origins, unauthenticated/unauthorized mutations, cross-project/path escapes, oversized input and arbitrary command/state-write attempts are rejected before unsafe effects. Secrets do not appear in responses/logs.
- [ ] **API-AC-09 — Contract and consumer compatibility:** API/error/event schemas are documented/versioned; an independent client contract test and CLI parity tests exercise the shared service behavior. Public package/asset consumption is aligned with the migration epic rather than source-tree internals.
- [ ] **API-AC-10 — Later adapters stay replaceable:** Document and test the execution/persistence/provider/transport boundaries needed for remote and scheduled callers without duplicating authority, assuming distributed safety, or silently enabling remote access. Later deployment decisions are explicitly recorded.
- [ ] **API-AC-11 — Normal self-hosted feature delivery:** The eventual child implementations use this repository's supported native workflow and preserve actual assignment/run, exact-revision validation, independent review, PR/CI and controlled-completion evidence under current governance. Neither this feature nor its companion is designated as a canary task; test fixtures are not represented as live delivery proof.
- [ ] **API-AC-12 — End-to-end acceptance and operations:** A documented walkthrough and automated integration scenarios cover conversation → revision/review → publication → authorized execution → review/rework → completion/blocked recovery → evidence inspection. Retain failures, rollback/restart instructions and all required repository checks against the implementation revision.

## Verification and rollout plan

This is a test plan, not a claim that tests have run for unimplemented functionality.

- Contract/unit tests for session revisions, plan validation and policy; golden schema fixtures for accepted/rejected plan/task/API payloads.
- Service and localhost integration tests using an independent client, deterministic fake/manual providers, real local persistence and a temporary Git repository. Cover stale plan acceptance, duplicate sends/start requests, restart during publication/execution, failed review, changed head, unauthorized merge attempts and disconnect/reconnect.
- Reuse repository safety practices [BP-001/BP-002](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/94a7a50ce0977112d20f8b2735dd88cebac61cfe/docs/development/best-practices.md): inspect rejected-action side effects, and where practical prove critical tests detect removal of their guard. Keep fixture evidence distinct from actual feature PR/review/CI evidence.
- Validate existing CLI/library consumers, schema-version compatibility, real required checks, and current Node/Windows/POSIX behavior where affected. Run the repository's applicable build/test/schema/contract suites; do not invent a universal coverage threshold.
- Introduce the service additively with local-only exposure and existing CLI compatibility. Stop/drain writers before rollback; preserve journals, accepted plans and append-only evidence. Do not downgrade across incompatible state schemas without an explicit supported migration.
- Completion requires an acceptance-to-evidence map and reviewed operational docs, not merely an HTTP server or a successful demo.

## Decisions for the later subtask-planning session

1. Choose the first planning provider/adapter and the bounded context it may read. The current local/manual execution adapter is not automatically a conversational planner.
2. Agree the exact plan envelope, draft storage/privacy/retention, repository artifact layout, and whether GitHub issue synchronization is needed in the first release.
3. Choose HTTP framework, client/schema tooling, polling versus replayable event transport, and the local authorization bootstrap without weakening the service/domain boundary.
4. Set the first supported project/workspace registration and execution-selection model, resource limits, and supported OS/runtime matrix.
5. Resolve bootstrap readiness against current authoritative evidence and confirm sequencing with the migration contract. Do not infer cutover from stale docs or closed checkboxes.

**No child issues have been created. No code, PR, package release, repository migration or feature execution has been performed by this planning issue.**

title: [BOOT-037] CLI workflow driver: issue intake, self-contained packets, automatic imports and error recovery
body:
## Objective

Provide a supported general-purpose CLI driver that runs **any eligible registered task** through the existing workflow using the existing manual role handoffs:

task selection/assignment → Developer packet → deterministic validation → required independent QA/Architect/UAT packets → PR/CI → merge readiness → explicitly authorized controlled merge → DONE → completed reconciliation.

Operators must be able to paste GitHub issue Markdown (or save it in an intake folder), receive a self-contained packet, paste that packet into a fresh agent chat without additional explanatory context, and save the response in an inbox for automatic validated import and continuation. The same exchange must handle clarification, errors and legal rework. Operators must not need to write JavaScript, hand-author config/request JSON, reconstruct chat history, or restart the workflow from scratch.

“Any task” still means a schema-valid native task definition with satisfied dependencies, canonical branch, scope, validators and required review roles. This issue now includes an intake/preparation layer that converts operator-selected issue Markdown into that validated definition and its config/request. Pasting an issue does not by itself establish eligibility, assignment, publication or merge authority.

**Parent:** #1  
**Task ID:** BOOT-037  
**Canonical branch:** `bootstrap/boot-037-general-workflow-driver`  
**Integration target:** `main`  
**Related:** #29 (orchestration engine), #30 (resume/idempotency), #31 (manual adapter), #35 (canary), #76 (UAT context repair)

## Current implementation and gaps

Analysis baseline: [main at fbc46888ce0b](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/commit/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc), inspected 2026-11-08. These are implementation findings, not test-pass or cutover claims.

| Surface | Present today | Implementation still needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| General driver | [Orchestration engine](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/src/orchestration-engine/orchestration-engine.ts) and local composition factory; [CLI command table](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/src/cli/commands.ts) still reserves `agent orchestrate`. | Supported CLI setup, intake, run/watch, status and resume; no custom host. |
| Issue → task/config/request | [Registry](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/docs/TASK_REGISTRY.md) only loads `tasks/definitions/*.task.json`; [task schema](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/schemas/v1/task.schema.json) requires scope, branch, dependencies, criteria, validators and roles. | Markdown ingestion, missing-field clarification, reusable repository profile, validated registration and generated stable request identities. No issue-Markdown importer exists on this baseline. |
| Fresh-chat handoff | [Manual provider](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/src/local-agent-adapter/file-manual-agent-provider.ts) already exports complete compiled role context, instructions and immutable result binding. | A copy-ready handoff containing repository/workspace instructions and the exact response schema/template. Current instructions refer to a separate result-schema file; packet-only usability needs an explicit acceptance test. |
| Response inbox | [Manual CLI](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/src/cli/manual.ts) requires packet ID, response file and exchange path. The provider polls only canonical imported result files. | Watch arbitrary incoming response filenames, route by validated binding, import atomically, issue receipts, and continue the workflow. Dropping raw output into the canonical exchange is not supported. |
| Errors and rework | [Run journal](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/src/orchestration-engine/run-store.ts) persists stages/failures; the engine throws infrastructure/precondition errors or returns STOPPED. Validation failure and review rework still need explicit intervention. [Recovery](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/docs/RECOVERY.md) preserves history and requires explicit authorization for administrative repair. | Durable driver-level waiting states plus self-contained error/clarification packets and typed repair responses. Recheck authoritative prerequisites before continuation; do not erase failure evidence. |
| PR and next task | [Canary host](https://github.com/Brain-Crumbs/IPTFantasyFootball/blob/fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc/scripts/canary.mjs) supplies PR/publication/merge guards but fixes CANARY-001, its branch, issue and a one-task registry. The general engine evaluates readiness and merges through its controller; it does not create/update a PR. | General PR composition and an explicit next-task handoff after DONE, reusing the repository profile and existing selection rules. |

BOOT-036/#76 addresses UAT submission for contract-bearing tasks. Verify its actual implementation on the chosen base; do not hide regressions by clearing task contracts in driver fixtures.

## Dependencies and operating authority

Verify the existing BOOT-006–029 workflow primitives and BOOT-030–032 diagnostics/recovery capabilities are present on authoritative main, plus the BOOT-036/#76 fix before claiming full acceptance for contract-bearing tasks. These are historical bootstrap dependencies, not permission to fabricate native DONE records.

Read AGENTS.md, CONSTITUTION.md, BOOTSTRAP.md, #1 and this issue before implementation. Preserve the manual-bootstrap assignment regime until explicit cutover. This issue authorizes the scoped driver implementation; it does not authorize live task selection unrelated to an operator assignment, publication, merge, recovery mutations or v1 cutover.

## Required operator experience

After a one-time guided repository setup:

1. **Paste or drop the issue.** Accept pasted Markdown through a documented CLI input mode (including stdin) and a configured `inbox/issues/` folder. Create the task/config/request from the selected issue and repository profile. If required information is missing or contradictory, emit a clarification packet through the same exchange instead of requiring hand-edited JSON.
2. **Copy one packet into a fresh chat.** Produce a clearly identified, copy-ready handoff containing everything needed to understand the assigned role, repository, task, scope, exact revision, permitted actions and response format. No extra narrative prompt is required. A pre-provisioned checkout/tool environment remains an explicit prerequisite; the packet must explain what to do if it is unavailable.
3. **Drop the response into `inbox/responses/`.** The running driver discovers it, validates and imports it through the existing adapter, records an import receipt, runs the owning gates and emits the next eligible packet automatically. The operator does not need to find packet hashes or run a separate import command.
4. **Handle errors the same way.** A recoverable failure or blocked prerequisite produces an error packet: copy to a fresh chat, save the structured repair response in the same inbox, and let the driver validate it and continue when the owning gate permits. The driver remains available; it does not require a new workflow or repeated setup.
5. **Hand off to the next task.** After verified DONE and reconciliation, show the next eligible candidate and a supported explicit next-task action, or accept the next issue in the intake folder. Reuse the repository profile but generate a distinct request for the next authorized task. Do not silently select/assign unrelated work.

Implement the reserved `agent orchestrate` surface. A possible shape is `init`, `prepare --stdin|--issue-file`, `watch`, `run`, `status`, `resume`, `next` and explicit publication/recovery operations. Final names may differ, but must be discoverable and exercised through the actual CLI. Include a scan-once path for scripting as well as the persistent watch loop. Preserve existing manual export/import/run commands.

Keep each engine run bounded to one selected task. An outer durable driver session may survive waits and link separately authorized rework attempts or subsequent tasks. Driver session state is coordination metadata, never a replacement for lifecycle/evidence authority.

**Automatic AI launch, vendor SDKs and desktop automation are not required.**

## In scope

### Inputs, registration and task binding
- Define strict, versioned, validated driver config/request contracts, examples and setup guidance. Reject unknown/invalid fields before workflow side effects.
- Config covers repository identity, integration target and required checks consistent with repository policy, paths, explicit role actors/policies, provider timeout/retry settings, task-to-issue PR metadata and publication/merge authorization.
- Credentials come from an explicit host environment source; never embed them in config examples, packets, reports or errors.
- Request preserves its original ownerId/runId/idempotencyKey/occurredAt. Preparation uses unique identities and exclusive creation; an existing file is inspected/reused, never overwritten to restart.
- Support multiple registered tasks and existing deterministic next-task/dependency rules. If an expected task ID is supplied to scope operator authorization, reject a mismatch before assignment or branch mutation; it must not bypass eligibility.
- Resume remains bound to the original task, assignment and stage identities, even if registry ordering changes or another task becomes eligible.
- Provide supported issue-intake registration of a non-canary task and its issue metadata as specified below. Registration must complete schema, dependency and authority checks before assignment; an exported manual request is never task registration.

### Guided setup and issue intake

- Create a reusable, versioned repository profile through a guided CLI or equivalent simple preparation command. Discover nonsecret facts such as repository root/remote where reliable, show the resulting values, and require explicit values for unresolved policy choices. Generate config/request files and exchange folders; no user-written JavaScript or UUID/hash assembly.
- Define a documented Markdown mapping/template covering task ID, title, objective, scope, canonical branch, dependencies, allowed paths, requirements/contracts, acceptance criteria, validation plan and required roles. Preserve the original Markdown and source hash, issue URL/number when supplied, and mapping diagnostics. Offline Markdown input must not depend on a live GitHub call.
- Handle free-form or incomplete issue text with an intake/clarification packet and a strict structured response for the unresolved fields or proposed task definition. Agent interpretations are proposals; deterministic schema/registry/DAG checks still decide whether registration is valid. Never invent missing dependencies, mark historical BOOT tasks DONE, silently drop scope/contracts, or assume a missing value means an empty list.
- Separate intake identity from task-run identity so errors before registration still have an addressable packet. A response cannot create arbitrary source files or execute commands from issue prose.
- Stage and validate the complete registration before making it eligible. Specify how generated task definitions/requirement artifacts become available on the exact source revision used by the compiler; account for dirty-tree checks and avoid partially registered tasks after interruption.
- Re-importing identical source/profile input reuses the prepared artifacts. Changed issue content, existing task-ID collisions and existing active runs produce an actionable conflict/change proposal, never overwrite a task definition or silently rebind an active request.
- Operator-selected intake is the authorization scope for preparation. Assignment still uses existing eligibility/assignment gates and the applicable bootstrap operating regime. Bulk synchronization or automatic execution of arbitrary GitHub issues is not required.

### Self-contained packets and automatic inbox import

- Retain the existing immutable role packet and exact gate-compiled context. Add a versioned companion handoff envelope or compatible renderer for copy/paste; do not edit canonical stored packet bytes or relax their validation. Keep role isolation when adding setup/repair context.
- Every handoff must identify its purpose (intake clarification, role work, repair, or completion/next action), repository/checkout expectations, task/issue/branch/revision where available, workflow/run/stage/packet binding, permitted actions, relevant context, and exactly where/how to return the result.
- Include the exact response envelope contract and a binding-filled response template with clearly marked fields for the agent's actual result. Include PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED and transport-error rules, findings/evidence requirements and timestamp format. Do not prefill a real judgment as PASS or require the operator to copy hashes manually.
- Document the supported saved-output format. Raw JSON must work. If accepting a single fenced JSON block copied from chat, unwrap it deterministically; reject multiple candidates or ambiguous surrounding output rather than guessing. Never evaluate pasted code.
- Keep `inbox/issues/`, `inbox/responses/`, outbound handoffs, accepted/failed input archives and the canonical manual exchange distinct. Final paths are configurable, printed by setup, and compatible with spaces and Windows/PowerShell.
- Scan on startup and while waiting; do not rely solely on filesystem events. Define a completion protocol for ordinary editor saves and slow file copies (e.g. readiness/stability checks plus atomic capture). Temporary/incomplete files must not be imported or trigger repeated error packets.
- Route results by versioned envelope and immutable binding, not filename or “most recent packet.” Validate repository/session ownership and expected pending work, then call the existing import API for role results. An imported response does not itself grant lifecycle/merge authority.
- Produce durable receipts identifying accepted/reused/rejected input, packet/task/stage, diagnostic and next action. Identical duplicate drops are no-ops; conflicting, stale, unknown or wrong-role responses preserve the originals and create a repairable rejection without terminating the watcher.
- Serialize workflow mutations with existing locks; two watchers must not import/advance twice or steal each other's execution tokens. Recover across a crash between accepted-result publication, receipt persistence and gate continuation by reconciling authoritative records.
- Persist a session manifest binding profile, intake, config/request, pending packets, attempts and receipts. Restarting the process performs a startup scan and resumes/reconciles authorized pending work without rerunning setup or reconstructing state from chat.

### Error packets, repair responses and continued operation

- Add strict versioned diagnostic/repair packet and response schemas separate from semantic review results. Cover preparation/schema/registration errors, rejected imports, context/gate exceptions, validation/review failures, transient provider/GitHub failures, CI/publication/authorization waits and exhausted retries.
- A packet includes a stable diagnostic ID, original intake/task/session/run/stage/packet identities as available, exact revision and relevant hashes, redacted error/log excerpts, authoritative state/evidence references, known completed work, the unresolved prerequisite, permitted repair scope, response schema/template and continuation conditions. Missing initial config must still yield a usable diagnostic to a safe output location or stdout; report inability to persist honestly.
- Catch per-input and per-workflow errors at the driver boundary. Persist a waiting/error state and deduplicated packet, continue listening for responses and keep status usable. A single malformed response must not shut down the service or block unrelated intake inspection. Infrastructure corruption must suspend unsafe mutations while diagnostics remain available when possible.
- Prevent repeated unchanged diagnostics and unbounded repair loops. Persist retry budgets and diagnostic generations; a malformed repair response gets a linked rejection without overwriting the prior packet. Slow manual chat work is waiting, not a continuously consumed infrastructure retry budget.
- Importing a repair response is a typed proposal or evidence of an action, not an arbitrary command runner, approval, or assertion that the problem is fixed. Permit only documented operations; re-read the exact source/state/remote facts and rerun the owning checks before continuing.
- **Same-attempt resume:** malformed unaccepted results may be corrected against the original packet; recoverable waits/infrastructure failures resume the original request/run/key/actor/context after preconditions are restored. Keep durable attempt counts; do not blindly retry an exhausted budget.
- **New judgment/rework:** accepted ERROR/CANCELLED responses and semantic FAIL/BLOCKED results remain immutable. Use the existing legal rework/recovery gates and separately authorized assignment transfer where required. Generate and link a successor request/packet only when a genuinely new attempt is permitted; retain predecessor history and revalidate/review the resulting revision. The outer driver session continues so the operator does not manually rebuild configs or “start over.”
- **Administrative actions:** lock release, assignment transfer, reset and emergency repair retain their existing host authorization, exact-hash and quiescence requirements. The driver must suspend/drain affected writers and require the prescribed external-session verification before applying such recovery; it may then resume its watch loop. A repair agent cannot authorize itself.
- **External prerequisites:** pending CI may be rechecked with bounded polling; missing credentials, publication, human authorization or out-of-scope code defects produce an actionable packet and remain waiting until actually resolved. Do not fabricate an agent fix for a human-only decision.
- Cancellation and unrecoverable host failures may stop the process. Preserve sufficient state for restart/reconciliation; the requirement is no routine workflow teardown or loss of progress, not a promise to survive power loss or unwritable storage without restarting a process.

### Composition and manual handoffs
- Reuse existing engine, provider, validation/review/rework gates, stores and GitHub adapters. The driver coordinates them; it does not recreate their decisions.
- Honor each task's actual required review roles, including supported subsets and tasks with requirements, affected contracts and dependency contracts.
- Distinct actor labels and externally enforced policies remain explicit operator boundaries. Fresh role contexts are required; labels alone prove neither independence nor permission enforcement.
- Developer may commit a new revision. Its transport binding stays at invocation identity; validators and later reviewers bind to actual final source HEAD.
- Clean-source/exact-revision checks prevent a review or PR action from certifying uncommitted changes or source drift.
- Manual imports retain immutable identity/context/policy checks and honest PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/error semantics. No synthetic role PASS or automatic retry of a terminal judgment.
- Human progress remains usable during waits; `--json` retains the CLI's machine-readable envelope, with progress on a separate documented channel.

### PR, CI and controlled merge
- Integrate the existing PR lifecycle adapter: create or reuse/update the single canonical PR for the selected task and target branch. Validate issue/branch/head identity; conflicting PRs fail explicitly.
- Expose the publication boundary clearly. Either support an explicitly authorized non-force push or pause with exact instructions and verify the remote head afterward. Never leave an unexplained “missing PR” dead end.
- New PRs remain draft unless separately authorized for ready-for-review conversion. Never treat draft creation as completed review or task acceptance.
- Missing/pending/failing/wrong-head CI returns an actionable stop. Same-request resume rereads readiness for the exact head without repeating completed role work.
- Require separate host authorization identifying the exact repository, PR number and full source SHA before a fresh controlled merge. Unspecified/mismatched authorization cannot merge; input approval fields are not a substitute for readiness or an authenticated approval service.
- Only the existing controlled-merge controller confirms merge evidence, releases the original assignment and advances MERGED/DONE. Recheck remote head and preserve interrupted-merge reconciliation.

### Resume, evidence and diagnostics
- Preserve existing journals, retry budgets, execution locks and immutable evidence. Detect incompatible config/policy/context changes under an existing run and reject rather than silently rebinding.
- Document which separately authorized operational fields may change for resume (for example exact merge authorization) without changing the original role/request identity.
- Cancellation stops waiting cooperatively and drains state-changing gates; explain that external role sessions may continue and require separate termination.
- Report stage, task, revision, result/stop reason and evidence/report paths. Retain before/during/after observations without presenting diagnostic clarity as approval.
- Re-running DONE reconciles without another role invocation, merge or completed evidence record.
- Failed reviews and failed validation emit the repair/rework handoff above and expose supported continuation through the existing legal gates. Never delete a journal, reset counters, invent an unlinked replacement run, or automatically apply administrative recovery without its required authority.

## Out of scope

- Automatic agent/session launching, vendor-specific AI integrations or a web UI.
- Replacing the lifecycle engine, broad scheduler/concurrent task execution, or weakening review/evidence semantics. A bounded driver session and legal rework composition are in scope.
- Bulk GitHub synchronization or unattended assignment/execution of arbitrary issues. Operator-selected Markdown intake, validated preparation and registration are explicitly in scope.
- Weakening dependency checks, branch protection, CI policy, exact-head binding or merge authorization.
- Mutating the stopped CANARY-001 run or overwriting its packets, requests, evidence or assignments.
- Implementing #76 inside this issue as an untracked workaround.
- Declaring canary acceptance or Bootstrap v1 cutover from fixture success.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh operator completes guided setup once, then pastes an issue or drops its Markdown in the intake folder; task/config/request and the next valid handoff are generated without editing JSON or writing a host script.
- [ ] Incomplete/contradictory Markdown produces a clarification packet; importing its response completes validated preparation without fabricating fields, dependencies or completion state.
- [ ] A fresh agent with the documented repository/tool access receives only the emitted handoff, with no additional explanatory prompt, and can return an importable response. Test normal role, clarification and repair packets.
- [ ] Dropping a raw response in the inbox automatically produces a validated import receipt and the next eligible stage/handoff. No packet-ID lookup or per-response import command is required.
- [ ] Malformed, partial, duplicate, conflicting, wrong-task/role/revision and stale responses cannot corrupt authoritative state, shut down the watcher or overwrite prior results.
- [ ] Representative setup, import, provider, validation, review and PR/CI failures emit actionable error packets; the same copy/paste/drop loop reaches the legal continuation or an explicit authorization wait without rebuilding the workflow.
- [ ] An accepted terminal outcome remains immutable. Required rework creates an auditable successor attempt through existing gates while keeping the driver session and predecessor evidence.
- [ ] Watcher restart and duplicate invocation reconcile pending intake/import/gate work without duplicate assignment, evidence, PR or merge; source/policy changes cannot silently rebind pending work.
- [ ] DONE presents the explicit next-task handoff using the reusable profile; a distinct task request is created only after operator selection/authorization.

- [ ] `agent orchestrate` is implemented, discoverable in help, and no longer returns COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for supported operations.
- [ ] A documented config/request can run an arbitrary eligible registered task without source edits or a custom host script; no CANARY-001/BOOT-033 branch, marker or issue number is hard-coded.
- [ ] In a multi-task registry, selection honors dependencies and authorization scope; resume stays with the original assignment.
- [ ] Full gate-compiled manual packets are produced in the correct order and imported through the existing CLI. A persisted Developer result alone never substitutes for deterministic validation.
- [ ] Nonempty requirements/contracts and dependency contracts work through UAT, including the #76 regression.
- [ ] A complete supported path exists from reviewed source to canonical PR, exact-head CI and authorized controlled merge, with actionable pauses at external prerequisites.
- [ ] Authorization, source/remote drift, failed/stale evidence, wrong packet binding and terminal role rejection all fail closed without bypassing their owning gate.
- [ ] Interrupted waits, concurrent invocation, resumable failures and lost merge responses preserve original identities/history and never duplicate a merge.
- [ ] DONE followed by same-key reconciliation leaves authoritative completed evidence unchanged.
- [ ] CLI output, exit codes, config/request schemas, Windows/PowerShell and POSIX examples are documented and tested; secrets do not appear in output/artifacts.
- [ ] Existing canary and other CLI behavior remain compatible. A fresh operator can complete the documented manual-handoff sequence without writing JavaScript.
